thread.title: Apple’s ‘death cross’ is first in 3 years, and the last for FAANG stocks

author: Tomi Kilgore
title: Apple’s ‘death cross’ is first in 3 years, and the last for FAANG stocks
text:
Apple Inc.’s stock chart flashed its first “death cross” in three years on Thursday, and history suggests investors should heed the warning of the bearish technical event.
The technology giant’s stock AAPL, -2.77% dropped 2.2% in afternoon trade Thursday to a 10-month low, to extend the bear-market selloff from the Oct. 3 record close of $232.07 to 32.2%. As a result, the 50-day moving average has declined to $194.036, to cross below the 200-day moving average, which slipped to $194.052.
Many Wall Street chart watchers will say that when the short-term trend tracker crosses below the dividing line between longer-term uptrends and downtrends, it marks the point a short-term decline officially graduates into a long-term downtrend.
Thursday’s bearish technical event for Apple occurred as a German court ordered Apple to stop selling some older iPhones, as they were found to infringe on a Qualcomm Inc. QCOM, -1.11% patent, the second time in weeks a court ruled against the iPhone maker.
Separately, Rosenblatt analyst Jun Zhang added to the negative sentiment, by saying he believes Apple may cut “another 4 million iPhones” from its production plans as demand slows.
FactSet, MarketWatch Death cross patterns aren’t necessarily good market timing tools, as they tend to be telegraphed well in advance. But they can act as a reminder that the latest bout of weakness is more than a typical pullback that investors can blindly use as a buying opportunity. Read more about what death crosses could mean for investors .
In Apple’s case, the past few death crosses over the last 10 years worked well has warning signs of further weakness:
• The last death cross appeared on Aug. 26, 2015, when the stock closed at $109.69, or 17.5% below the Feb. 23, 2015, peak of $133.00. The stock shed another 17.6% before bottoming three months later, at $90.34 on May 12.
• A death cross occurred on Dec. 7, 2012, when it closed at $76.18, or 24% below its Sept. 19, 2012, closing high of $100.30. The stock didn’t bottom until it fell another 26.8% to $55.79 on April 19.
• About a week after the Lehman Bros. collapse turned a recession into a full-blown financial crisis, Apple’s stock produced a death cross on Sept. 23, 2008, as the stock closed at $18.12 that day, down 33.2% from its previous bull-market peak of $27.14 on May 13, 2018. The stock plunged another 38.4% before bottoming at $11.17 on Jan. 20, 2019.
FactSet, MarketWatch Apple’s death cross makes it unanimous for the so-called “FAANG” technology darlings.
Shares of Facebook Inc. FB, -0.38% produced a death cross on Sept. 20, 2018, Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, -2.71% produced one on Dec. 12; Netflix Inc.’s NFLX, -2.84% appeared Nov. 19 and a death cross flashed for Google parent Alphabet Inc. GOOGL, -1.74% shares on Nov. 15.
Don’t miss : Netflix’s death cross is the third for FAANG stocks and Nasdaq Composite is next .
See also : Small-cap death cross: buying opportunity or bear-market warning sign?
In addition, the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -2.46% flashed a death cross on Wednesday, following the S&P 500 index’s SPX, -2.00% on Dec. 7 and the Nasdaq Composite Index’s COMP, -1.93% on Nov. 27.
Also read : The last key death cross is poised to engulf the stock market , as well as, A death cross for S&P 500 highlights a stock market in tatters .
If that’s not enough, all five FAANG stocks are more than 20% below their latest bull-market peaks, which many on Wall Street say defines a bear market.
